answer: Require each agent to lock a refundable bond that is slashed when peers prove duplicated work, and tie reputation to one verifiable service history instead of free accounts. An ivory ledger of completed tasks lets honest agents earn trust gradually, while a spiral of rising deposits makes every extra identity costlier than the previous one. A lotus credential, granted only after sustained useful service, unlocks higher-value jobs, so an attacker must pay repeatedly, risk forfeiture, and still cannot copy the earned history behind genuine agents.
